record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Dynamical Systems
record.context_brief: Sparse periodic orbits in convex Hamiltonian dynamics
record.original_question: Let H₀(r) be a real-analytic strictly convex superlinear Hamiltonian on T^n × R^n with ∂H₀/∂r(0) = 0 and n ≥ 2. Can one find a real-analytic one-parameter perturbation H_ε(θ,r) = H₀(r) + εH′(θ,r,ε) and some small ε₀ such that, on the energy surface H_{ε₀}^{-1}(1), the periodic orbits of the Hamiltonian flow are not dense?

evidence.quote: Question. Can one find a Cω-family Hε(θ; r) = H0(r)+εH′0(θ; r; ε) ... such that for some ε0 small on H−1ε0(1), the periodic orbits of the Hamiltonian flow of Hε0 are not dense ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ and let $H_0 : \mathbb{T}^n \times \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, $(\theta, r) \mapsto H_0(r)$, be a real-analytic Hamiltonian depending only on the action variable $r$, that is strictly convex (i.e., the Hessian $\partial^2 H_0/\partial r^2$ is positive definite everywhere) and superlinear (i.e., $H_0(r)/|r| \to \infty$ as $|r| \to \infty$), and that satisfies $\partial H_0/\partial r(0) = 0$. Consider real-analytic one-parameter perturbations of the form
$$H_\varepsilon(\theta, r) = H_0(r) + \varepsilon\, H'(\theta, r, \varepsilon),$$
where $H' : \mathbb{T}^n \times \mathbb{R}^n \times (-\varepsilon_*, \varepsilon_*) \to \mathbb{R}$ is real-analytic. Endow $\mathbb{T}^n \times \mathbb{R}^n$ with the standard symplectic form $\sum_i d\theta_i \wedge dr_i$, so that $H_\varepsilon$ generates a Hamiltonian flow.

Question: Does there exist such a perturbation $H'$ and some $\varepsilon_0 > 0$ (arbitrarily small) such that on the energy surface $H_{\varepsilon_0}^{-1}(1)$ the periodic orbits of the Hamiltonian flow of $H_{\varepsilon_0}$ are not dense?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches on density of periodic orbits in perturbed convex Hamiltonian systems return general results on existence and multiplicity of periodic orbits on convex energy surfaces, but no source confirming a resolution of this specific question about whether a real-analytic one-parameter perturbation of an integrable convex Hamiltonian can fail to have dense periodic orbits on a near-energy surface. Status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Convex Hamiltonian energy surfaces and their periodic trajectories
status_evidence.snippet: Symplectic invariants for convex Hamiltonian energy surfaces and their periodic trajectories satisfy nontrivial relations and yield multiplicity results.
status_evidence.claim: Existing results on convex Hamiltonian energy surfaces address existence/multiplicity of periodic orbits but do not address density under analytic perturbation.

status_evidence.title: Periodic orbits and global surfaces of section in Hamiltonian systems
status_evidence.snippet: Hamiltonian flow on a three-dimensional strictly convex energy surface possesses a global surface of section of disc type, with 2 or infinitely many periodic orbits.
status_evidence.claim: Known density-type statements pertain to specific low-dimensional convex settings, not the higher-dimensional analytic perturbative setting in question.
